title: Interventions to increase appropriate anticoagulation in atrial fibrillation: an umbrella review to inform a health board's choice
abstract: Objective: to compare the evidence from published reviews on interventions that increase appropriate anticoagulation in adults with atrial fibrillation. Design: umbrella review with a registered protocol, AMSTAR 2 appraisal and overlap assessment. Outcomes: appropriate anticoagulation (primary), stroke, major bleeding and decisional conflict. Results will follow the search and extraction.
introduction: About one in five eligible people on the health board's atrial fibrillation lists has no anticoagulant prescription, and several interventions compete for funding. A preliminary in-app search returned no records, so the evidence base must be assembled by a full search.
methods: Reviews are identified through a library search of four databases and two review registers, screened in duplicate, appraised with AMSTAR 2 and mapped in a citation matrix. Effects are tabulated by intervention level with certainty ratings; an informed decline is reported as a legitimate outcome.
results: No data have been extracted yet. The report will present the flow of reviews, the citation matrix and corrected covered area, AMSTAR 2 ratings, and effects by intervention level.
discussion: The discussion will state which intervention types have the most certain effect on prescribing, what is and is not known about strokes and bleeding, and where the register's population is missing from the evidence.
limitations: Dependent on existing reviews; overlap and review quality limit certainty; recent primary studies may be missed.
conclusion: To be written after synthesis; it will not present a prescribing gain as a reduction in strokes.
summary: PRIOR-structured draft with results left empty until extraction.
